summary: Test-writing phase for issue #39. Added the solver parity suite that replays the upstream color_matching golden-vector corpus (12 scenarios, exact scores/selection/ties/exclusions) against WeightedSquaredErrorScorer and CompositionSolver, added the OpenAPI contract suite that pins the vendored published document (currently red: the document is not vendored yet), pinned the PaletteAPIClient behavior the generated-client migration must preserve, pinned the disk-cache/offline-fallback data path, and documented both external artifacts under docs/. Fixed two pre-existing compile errors that made `swift test` unbuildable (PaletteAPIClientTests.swift: implicit self capture and a missing `await`). Local verification ran with Swift 6.1.2 on Linux: 228 tests executed, 3 failures (the red-phase OpenAPI contract tests), 225 passing.

references.note: Fails with "The published OpenAPI document is not vendored in the package" - the document and the generated client are implementation work, not test work.
Pins PrinterProfilesResponse/PrinterProfile/ColorsResponse shapes the generated types must match.
Pins the bearerAuth security scheme the generated client must send.

verification.notes: swift-openapi-generator/swift-openapi-runtime adoption and the PaletteAPIClient migration are implementation-phase deliverables; this phase only specifies them.

references.note: GET /api/v1/printer_profiles, GET method, Accept: application/json.
GET /api/v1/colors?printer_profile_id=N.
ColorsResponse envelope (printer_profile + colors + responses) decodes unchanged.
503 -> PaletteAPIError.badStatus(503); the UI keeps telling failures apart.
Unreadable body -> PaletteAPIError.malformedResponse.
401 -> PaletteAPIError.unauthorized (re-authentication path preserved).

verification.notes: swift test --filter PaletteAPIClientTests: 9 tests, 0 failures (Linux, Swift 6.1.2).

references.note: A fetch decoded from the server envelope stays servable offline: domain colors convert, unmeasured channels stay missing, and fetchedAt (the offline-stale badge date) survives the disk round-trip.
Per-server cache namespaces: allEntries(serverBaseUrl:) only returns the requesting server's profiles (the cached-profile fallback source).
A profile cached from another server is a miss, so servers never share offline palettes.

verification.notes: swift test --filter ProfileColorCacheTests: 70 tests, 0 failures (Linux, Swift 6.1.2).

references.note: isServingFromCache (the stale badge) and the cached-profile picker live in the macOS app target; this container has no macOS/Xcode, so no runnable test could be written for them in this phase.

verification.notes: The data these UI paths consume (cached colors per server/profile, cached profile list, fetch date) is covered by AC-3; the app-level presentation and the 'serve cached profiles when the server is unreachable' decision remain unverified here and must be checked on macOS.

references.note: Committed copy of viamin/color_matching priv/parity/v1/corpus.json (upstream PR #112 for issue #111), 12 scenarios.
Every candidate of every scenario scores exactly like the server's scorer, .excluded included.
Selected index, selected hex color and error match the corpus exactly.
Tied-candidate set matches the corpus (tie evidence).
Every tie scenario resolves to the earliest tied candidate.
The full CompositionSolver (fast path the app uses) lands on the corpus winner.
A fully excluded palette yields no selection and no error.
Committed bytes still match the upstream artifact (FNV-1a fingerprint d29f7eebb0aa8010).

verification.notes: swift test --filter SolverParityCorpusTests: 9 tests, 0 failures (Linux, Swift 6.1.2). Mutation-checked: flipping the solver's tie-break to '<=' fails the tie scenarios; removing the scorer's exclusion rule fails the missing-measurement scenarios, so the suite is not vacuous.

references.note: Where the corpus lives upstream and in this repo, the contract it pins, and the exact refresh steps (including the fingerprint recomputation).
Where the published OpenAPI document lives, how to refresh it, and the API shape notes the PR description has to carry.

verification.notes: README.md is outside the paths this test-writing phase may change, so the README section the issue asks for is deferred to the implementation phase; the docs above carry the same content.

references.note: Findings recorded for the PR description: the app keeps GET /api/v1/colors?printer_profile_id=N while the server also publishes the profile-scoped GET /api/v1/printer_profiles/{id}/colors; responses is an open map keyed by light source with unmeasured sources absent; errors use {"errors":{"detail":...}}.

verification.notes: The pull request itself is created by the implementation run that lands the generated client.

references.note: 3 expected red-phase failures: the published OpenAPI document is not vendored in the package yet.

verification.notes: swift test (Swift 6.1.2, Linux): 228 tests executed, 3 failures - all three are the red-phase OpenAPI contract tests; the other 225 pass. Two pre-existing compile errors that blocked `swift test` entirely (implicit self capture and a missing `await` in PaletteAPIClientTests.swift) are fixed. `bin/lint` passes in this container (no Swift toolchain on the default PATH, so it skips the build); note that bin/lint's Linux harness excludes PaletteAPIClient.swift while still compiling PaletteAPIClientTests.swift, which is a pre-existing harness bug the implementation phase must fix together with the new package dependencies.
